#
# mint rows: a numeral inside a minted sentence, and the form that reads it —
#   pattern:<id>   a COUNTED_CLAIMS phrasing, re-derived from the sentence's records
#   declared:<id>  the sentence names its own predicate (COUNT_PREDICATES), re-derived
#   record         a number the sentence read out of a value it declares
#   quoted         a fragment the sentence reproduces verbatim out of the record
#   transcribed    the sentence declares no reads at all, so it computed nothing —
#                  a seeded fixture line, minted so the record owns its characters
#   form:<id>      a declared non-count shape: a clock time, a date, an amount
#                  of money, a percentage
#   measured       a duration, re-derived from the two record timestamps the
#                  sentence named — not a shape. A duration used to be filed as
#                  form:duration, which asked whether `3h` LOOKED like a duration
#                  and never what it was a duration FROM (round 17, D1).
#   UNREAD         no check on this page can read it. This is a defect and the
#                  page's console says so on the paint that renders it.
#   UNMEASURED     a duration the sentence measured nothing for, and
#   MISMEASURED    one whose two named timestamps no longer give it. Both are
#                  defects and the console says so on the paint that renders them.
# page rows: a numeral in no minted sentence — row counters, message counters,
#   page furniture, and record text the page reprints outside a mint. Not an error
#   list: a count of rows is not a claim about a record. This is the set
#   CONVENTIONS.md used to name from memory, and was wrong about, for a round.
#   The toast is excluded: it is minted, and painted with textContent because it
#   is raised after its render — checkToastInvariant() re-reads it.
#
# Digits are normalised to `#`: the claim is about FORMS, not about values.
# subject: the union over every state reachable in 0, 1 or 2 writes.
#
